reply_text:
㊥ (Zai frozen) I see it too: none of the three Zai jobs has logged anything for several minutes. Less is lost than it looks, though. Two of their long runs are separate processes that keep going without the agents:
- zai-3's re-probe has done 12 of 34 rows and writes its results straight into the progress table.
- zai-1's final probe is still rebuilding: the byte check, then `addParserTokens`.

I'll do the rest of zai-1's job myself.

㊢ (zai-1, the `ite` condition fix) zai-1 had already committed its test (`90382ab`) and fix (`69af4db`). I ran the test at the old base: the positive case fails there and passes with the fix. The fix adds the port's missing elaborators for `let_mvar%` and `wait_if_type_mvar%`, following `BuiltinTerm.lean:118-146`. A later `?m` then turns into the stored `==` term. When the type is still unknown, the port refuses rather than guessing, which matches Lean's postponement.

When its probe finishes I'll finish the review, run the gates, and merge if they hold.

㊟ (one path in zai-1's fix) If the compiled value has no term, the fix rebuilds one by reading the syntax as a type. I don't think Lean does anything like that, so I'll check whether that path runs in the real code before merging.

㊢ (zai-2, `x.f` on local variables) zai-2 had only just started: two uncommitted files in `/tmp/mfs-dotfix`, no commits. I'll leave it until either Zai resets or codex-4 or codex-6 finishes. Whichever comes first gets the job; the brief stays the same.

🈳 (when Zai resets) I don't know when the five-hour window started, so I can't say when it resets.

㊢ (watching for results) Nothing will wake me when the two background runs finish. I'll check them at the next wake, which will be one of the Codex jobs reporting back or a park deadline.

㊢ (open jobs)

| agent | job | state |
|---|---|---|
| codex-6 | `tuple`/`nomatch` | running, park `park-82be1026` |
| codex-4 | `replaceM` export alias | running, park `park-83c6c953` |
| zai-1 | `ite` condition fix | frozen; its probe still running; I'm finishing it |
| zai-2 | `x.f` on local variables | frozen, barely started; on hold |
| zai-3 | re-probe | frozen; the batch is still running (12/34) |

(Codex back on queued fixes) Both Codex jobs have started; neither hit a capacity error.
- **codex-6:** the builtin `tuple`/`nomatch` fix, 3 rows (`invoke-…49c00a01`, park `park-82be1026`).
- **codex-4:** the export-alias fix in match-pattern normalization, for `replaceM` (`invoke-…fc307795`, park `park-83c6c953`).

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what each job must do)
- **codex-6:** take builtin syntax such as `tuple` and `nomatch` from the compiler's own registry before asking the target file's imports. The set of builtins has to come from Lean's registrations, not from a list of names. A non-builtin kind must still be rejected as it is now.
- **codex-4:** make match patterns resolve names through one of the port's existing Lean-faithful resolvers, such as the one zai-2 just rewrote. It must not add another resolver, and must say which one it used.
